subject: Scaling prior auth ML — annotation infra at Cohere
text:
Hi [NAME]​, 

I read Cohere's recent post on AI-powered prior auth reducing care abandonment - great articulation of why this problem matters clinically, not just operationally. 

Given the complexity of parsing scanned clinical faxes and routing them through SID-based models, I was curious how your team's thinking about annotation and QA infra. We've been working with ML teams at Elevance and Truveta tackling similar document pipelines - helping them improve field-level extraction by building better feedback loops, and speed up iteration cycles with structured HITL flows. 

Would be curious to swap notes on what you're seeing - especially around ambiguous formats, upstream noise, or model drift across provider forms. Would you be open to a quick 20-min chat next week?

subject: Prior auth ML — scaling annotation infra to match ambition
text:
Hi [NAME]​, 

Just read your team's piece on reducing care abandonment via AI-powered prior auth - compelling case for how better automation can directly improve clinical outcomes. 

Given how core unstructured faxes still are to the pipeline, I was curious how you're thinking about the infra that supports annotation and QA at scale. We've been partnering with teams at Elevance and Truveta facing similar challenges - helping them improve extraction quality by tightening the feedback loop between messy inputs, human-in-the-loop workflows, and model iteration. 

If useful, happy to share what we're seeing work well across comparable high-volume, high-stakes ML deployments. Would you be open to a brief 20-min chat next week Tuesday or Thursday?

subject: Challenges with Labelbox for improving model performance | Working with Carbon Robotics
text:
Hi [NAME]​, 

Saw the recent news of xarvio SCOUTING reaching 6M farmers and the team's focus on the curation of the field / satellite images as critical for maintaining xarvio's 90% accuracy advantage. 

I've been working with a number of precision agriculture teams (e.g. Carbon Robotics, John Deere, Aigen etc) who started with Labelbox but were facing issues with scaling across different crop varieties / geographic conditions and were looking to find a way to surface edge cases from massive datasets and improve model performance. 

Given xarvio's expansion and competitive pressure in digital farming, curious how you're prioritizing which data gets expert annotation versus routine inference. Would you be open to a 20-minute chat? I'm usually free Tuesdays/Thursdays.

subject: Scaling ML infrastructure post-Series C
text:
Hi [NAME]​, 

Saw the recent Series C - congrats to you and the team. Noticed part of the raise is going toward enhancing AI capabilities across the member experience, and was interested - are you investing in internal ML tooling or leaning more into off-the-shelf models? 

I lead a Retail AI team at Encord - we work with teams at companies like Flipkart, Ebay and Zoopla to accelerate vision and multimodal ML workflows. A lot of them hit friction when early AI use cases start to scale - especially around training data infrastructure, human feedback tooling, or annotation operations. 

If you're currently thinking about how to evaluate or scale any vision or fashion tagging models (e.g. inventory image workflows, look prediction, personalisation), would be glad to swap notes. 

Would you be open to a quick 20-min chat next week?
